nodes.label: AI co-mathematician: Accelerating mathematicians with agentic AI
nodes.author: Daniel Zheng, Ingrid von Glehn, Yori Zwols, Iuliya Beloshapka, Lars Buesing, Daniel M. Roy, Martin Wattenberg, Bogdan Georgiev, Tatiana Schmidt, Andrew Cowie, Fernanda Viegas, Dimitri Kanevsky, Vineet Kahlon, Hartmut Maennel, Sophia Alj, George Holland, Alex Davies, Pushmeet Kohli
nodes.rationale: Introduces AI co-mathematician workbench for interactive mathematical research, emphasizing stateful collaboration, uncertainty management, and native mathematical artifacts.

nodes.label: Agentic AI Systems
nodes.rationale: Core architectural pattern: multi-agent systems with planning, tool use, memory, self-reflection, and iterative execution enabling multi-step workflows.

nodes.label: Uncertainty Management in AI Research
nodes.rationale: System architecture designed around lifecycle of uncertainty: tracks via version history, manages via compute-for-validation tradeoffs, communicates via inline highlighting and margin notes.

nodes.label: Embrace Mathematics Beyond Proofs
nodes.rationale: Design principle: genuine mathematical discovery involves complex mixture of activities beyond theorem proving including ideation, literature search, computational exploration, theory building.

nodes.label: Support Iterative Refinement of Intent
nodes.rationale: Design principle: discovery heavily dependent on continuous iteration and refinement; formulating right question requires extensive heuristic guesswork; flexible interface supports multiple exploration paths.

nodes.label: Produce Native Mathematical Artifacts
nodes.rationale: Design principle: center process around living 'working paper' with inline text and margin notes; track evolving state and visualize through native mathematical community formats.

nodes.label: Enable Asynchronous Interaction and Flexible Steering
nodes.rationale: Design principle: system operates as asynchronous team with messaging system allowing multiple specialized agents to work in parallel; user can intervene, bypass constraints, steer research at any time.

nodes.label: Manage Cognitive Load via Progressive Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Design principle: separate high-level intent from low-level execution by mirroring agent hierarchy; user primarily interacts with project coordinator, can drill down into specialized agents on demand.

nodes.label: Track, Manage, and Communicate Uncertainty
nodes.rationale: Design principle: architecture designed around lifecycle of uncertainty; tracks via version history, manages via compute-for-validation, communicates via inline highlighting and margin notes.

nodes.label: Preserve the History of Failed Explorations
nodes.rationale: Design principle: treat dead ends as first-class permanent outcomes; preserve 'negative space' of project history; knowing what doesn't work often as important as knowing what does.

nodes.label: AI co-mathematician System
nodes.rationale: Workbench for mathematicians to interactively leverage AI agents for open-ended research; provides stateful workspace with project coordinator agent delegating to specialized workstream coordinators.

nodes.label: Gemini Language Models
nodes.rationale: Underlying models powering AI co-mathematician; includes Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini Deep Think; system is harness designed for standard commercially available models without custom training.

nodes.label: FrontierMath Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Tier 4 benchmark with 50 problems crafted as short-term research projects by professors and postdocs; AI co-mathematician achieved 48% accuracy (23/48), new high score among all evaluated systems.

nodes.label: Internal Research Mathematics Evaluation
nodes.rationale: 100 unleaked research-level problems with code-checkable answers; AI co-mathematician achieved 87% vs 70% for Gemini Deep Think and 57% for Gemini 3.1 Pro.

nodes.label: Case Study: Kourovka Problem Resolution
nodes.rationale: M. Lackenby used AI co-mathematician to resolve Problem 21.10 from Kourovka Notebook; system created workstreams to prove and disprove result; human-AI back-and-forth crucial to resolution.

nodes.label: Case Study: Stirling Coefficients
nodes.rationale: G. Bérczi used system to investigate log-concavity of Stirling coefficients; system established proofs for two conjectures and provided computational evidence for unproven cases.

nodes.label: Case Study: Hamiltonian Systems Lemma
nodes.rationale: S. Rezchikov posed technical subproblem on Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms; system produced elegant proof that withstood careful checking; demonstrated value of reaching dead ends faster.

nodes.label: Reviewer-Pleasing Bias (False Consensus)
nodes.rationale: Iterative review process can converge to flawed argument where errors can no longer be detected by reviewer agents; violation of core principle of explicitly acknowledging uncertainty.

nodes.label: Intractable Disagreements (Non-Termination)
nodes.rationale: Iterative review process can fail to reach consensus and fail to terminate; loop degrades into increasingly hallucinated reasoning ('death spiral'); core issue of language models disagreeing remains.

nodes.label: System Autonomy Requires Ceding Control
nodes.rationale: Mathematical research inherently exploratory; predefined task planning often impossible; significant risk that model encounters unplanned difficulty; current models' judgment far behind human capabilities.

nodes.label: Semantic Meaning of Representations
nodes.rationale: Mathematicians associate well-typeset documents with rigor, but LLMs excel at formatting while struggling with logical verification; new interfaces needed to represent document characteristics intuitively.

nodes.label: Maintaining Signal-to-Noise in Literature
nodes.rationale: As AI systems become proficient at LaTeX and literature synthesis, community must manage potential influx of automated output; risk of rise in plausible but shallow, incremental, or subtly flawed papers.

nodes.label: Adapting Peer Review Ecosystem
nodes.rationale: AI can generate 20-page proof in minutes but human expert takes days to verify; if AI-assisted drafting becomes ubiquitous without auditable paper trails, heavy burden on volunteer peer review system.

hyperedges.label: Seven Core Design Principles for AI Co-Mathematician
